newsitem.title: USA: Ohio winter wheat harvest makes rapid progress.
newsitem.headline: Ohio winter wheat harvest makes rapid progress.

text.p: Hot, mostly dry weather helped to ripen winter wheat in Ohio and allow the harvest to make rapid progress after previous delays, according to the weekly crop update from the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.
The winter wheat harvest was 41 percent complete by Sunday, sharply up from just four percent a week earlier. It remained behind the five-year average of 63 percent.
The amount of winter wheat that was ripe rose to 86 percent from 34 percent a week earlier.
There were 6.9 days suitable for fieldwork during the week to Friday.

Ohio's average corn development stage for the majority of the corn was nine to 10 leaves fully emerged. Corn silked rose to four percent from one percent a week earlier. It remained nine days behind the five-year average of 22 percent.
Soybean blooming rose to 58 percent from 35 percent a week earlier and was five days ahead of the five-year average of 47 percent.
Topsoil moisture was seven percent very short, 41 percent short, 51 percent adequate and one percent surplus as of July 18.
